status_summary: Executive Order 14181 (signed 2025-01-24, published 2025-01-31) directs Reclamation to deliver more Central Valley Project water, including by increasing storage and conveyance, and to identify California water-supply and storage projects. On 2026-01-23 Interior approved the record of decision for the 1.5 million acre-foot Sites Reservoir, with Reclamation funding up to 25 percent of cost, and reported that operational changes under the order delivered more than 200,000 additional acre-feet of water to the Central Valley Project within a year, partly attributed to favorable hydrology. The order does not mention the 2018 western water memorandum, and no action on water control manuals, working-group consolidation, forecast-informed operations or WIFIA was found, so the match is partial and limited to California.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14181 signed, directing Reclamation to increase Central Valley Project water deliveries and identify storage projects (published 2025-01-31).
Interior approved the record of decision for the 1.5 million acre-foot Sites Reservoir, authorizing Reclamation to fund up to 25 percent of cost.

title: Expand western water storage and modernize reservoir operations at Reclamation
uncertainties: The 2018 memorandum is not in the order text, and a news search found no reinstatement. The Federal Register page for the order lists two later executive orders of 2026-01-23 (EO 14377 and EO 14378) as related notes; their content was not read, and one search did not identify them. The release attributes part of the added water to favorable hydrology rather than to the order alone. Reclamation's forecast-informed operations work was not found beyond a state council letter that was not relied on. Whether storage projects outside California advanced was not searched in detail.
